mainTopic: Rejecting the comparison to the גט case, reading הטעו as 'backed out,' and the ברייתא's rules for paying workers when a job falls through
overview: The גמרא first rejects the attempt to compare workers hired through a middleman to רב נחמן's ruling about a שליח carrying a גט. In that case the שליח cancelled his own agency completely, so it shows nothing about whose words the husband relies on. Then the גמרא offers a new reading of the משנה: the word הטעו (deceived) can mean חזרו (backed out of the deal). It proves this from a long ברייתא about hired workers. If either side backs out before work begins, there is only a complaint (תרעומת). If the workers came and found no work, they get the reduced pay of an idle worker. If they quit partway, the court values their work so that they do not gain from quitting, and רבי דוסא calculates this differently. When quitting would cause a loss and no replacements are available, the employer may hire others at their expense or trick them into finishing. Finally, רב and the גמרא discuss whether idle workers get any pay at all. The answer depends on whether the employer checked his field the night before, a distinction that רבא also uses and that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The comparison to the גט case is rejected, starting with the reverse case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the comparison does not work. It points out that a proof about whose words the husband relies on could only come from a different ruling, such as the reverse case.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare these? It would make sense if the opposite case had been taught: she said 'Receive my גט for me,' the שליח told the husband 'Your wife said: Bring me my גט,' and the husband said 'Here, as she said.' If רב נחמן had then ruled that she is divorced as soon as the גט reaches the שליח's hand, that would show the husband relies on her words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the earlier proof. It starts describing what kind of ruling would really prove that the husband relies on the wife's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא tried to learn from רב נחמן's גט case whether we follow the sender's words or the agent's words. Here it says a real proof would need a ruling where the גט takes effect according to one person's words. In this reverse case, a divorce at the שליח's hand would show the husband followed her words ('receive').

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? Is that the same? (a rejection of a comparison)
It would be fine / understandable if...
The opposite, the reverse case
Receive my גט for me (makes the שליח an agent of receiving)
Bring me my גט (makes him only a delivery agent)
This shows that, evidently

steps.confusionAlert: This reverse case is not a real ruling. The גמרא is describing what רב נחמן WOULD have needed to say for the earlier proof to work.

phrases.english: How can these be compared?!
It would be understandable if the opposite had been stated:
[She said:] 'Receive my get for me,'
and [the agent told the husband:] 'Your wife said: Bring me my get,'
and he says: 'Here it is, as she said.'

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh, in the name of Rav:
Once the get reaches his hand, she is divorced,
that would show he relies on her words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made just before this section, between the middleman case and רב נחמן's גט ruling
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The attempt to prove from רב נחמן's גט case whose words the sender relies on
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב נחמן's actual ruling does not make the גט take effect according to either person's words, so it cannot show whose words the husband relies on

steps.title: A second ruling that would have proven something
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds another possible ruling: if the divorce took effect when the גט reached her hand, that would show the husband relied on the שליח's words.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if he had ruled that she is divorced once the גט reaches her hand, that would show the husband relies on the שליח's words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second ruling that would have proven something. It is still building toward its point about the real case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A divorce only when the גט reaches her would mean the שליח acted as a delivery agent, which matches what he told the husband ('bring'). So that ruling would prove the husband followed the שליח's words. But רב נחמן actually ruled that she is not divorced at all, for a different reason, as the next step explains.

keyTerms.meaning: Or alternatively
Speech, words, statement
Relies on

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי: מִשֶּׁהִגִּיעַ גֵּט לְיָדָהּ מְגוֹרֶשֶׁת –
phrases.english: Or alternatively, [if he had ruled:] once the get reaches her hand, she is divorced –
that would show he relies on his words.
phrases.notes: 'His words' means the שליח's words, not the husband's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ruling that would have worked as a proof, alongside the one in step 1
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Only a ruling that makes the divorce take effect at a specific point would reveal whose words are relied on

steps.title: The real reason: the agent cancelled his own agency
steps.stepSummary: In רב נחמן's real case, she is not divorced because the שליח cancelled his agency completely. It has nothing to do with whose words the husband relies on.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there, the reason is that the שליח uprooted his agency completely. He was really telling the husband: 'I am an agent for receiving. I am not an agent for delivering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the true reason behind רב נחמן's ruling. That reason finishes off the earlier comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife made him a delivery agent, but he told the husband he would only be a receiving agent. That means he refused the job she gave him, so he is not really anyone's agent. This is why the divorce never takes effect, and so the case teaches nothing about whose words the husband follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Uprooted, cancelled
Agency, the job of being a שליח
Receiving (a גט on the woman's behalf)
Delivering, carrying (the גט to her)

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's גט case cannot be used for the middleman question. The שליח there fully cancelled his agency, so neither person's words decide anything.

phrases.english: But there, it is because the agent uprooted
phrases.notes: 'There' is רב נחמן's real case, where she is not divorced even when the גט reaches her.

phrases.english: his agency completely,
for he said to him: 'I am an agent for receiving,'
'I am not one for delivering.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָתָם מִשּׁוּם דְּעָקַר שָׁלִיחַ לִשְׁלִיחוּתֵיהּ לִגְמָרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After describing rulings that would have proven something, it explains what really happens in רב נחמן's case
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Closes the rejection of the comparison to the גט case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling there rests on the שליח cancelling his agency, not on whose words were relied upon

steps.title: New reading: 'deceived' means 'backed out'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a different way to read the משנה. This תנא uses the word הטעו (deceived) to mean חזרו (backed out of the deal).
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say this instead: this תנא also uses the word 'deceived' for 'backed out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a fresh explanation of the word הטעו in the משנה. It no longer reads it as a mix-up in the middleman's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא assumed 'they deceived each other' meant someone gave a wrong wage figure. Now it suggests the משנה simply means one side retracted, either the employer or the workers. That removes the need to ask whose words count.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces another answer)
A Sage of the משנה period / the author of a teaching
They backed out, retracted
They deceived, misled

phrases.english: If you want, say:
this Tanna also calls 'backed out'
by the name 'deceived,'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the middleman-and-agency line and gives a completely different reading of the משנה's word
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הטעו means one side misstated the wage terms
steps.terutzMaskana: הטעו can mean one side backed out of the agreement

steps.title: A ברייתא that uses 'deceived' for backing out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about hiring craftsmen. It uses 'deceived' for either side backing out and rules that there is only a complaint, with no money owed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: If someone hires craftsmen, and they deceived the employer, or the employer deceived them, they have nothing against each other except a complaint.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support its new reading of 'deceived.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's ruling fits a case of retracting before work began, as its next lines make clear. So 'deceived' here must mean backing out. That supports reading the משנה the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: Craftsmen, artisans
The employer, homeowner
A complaint, grievance (with no legal money claim)

phrases.english: As it was taught: One who hires craftsmen
and they deceived the employer,
or the employer deceived them –

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָהֶם זֶה עַל זֶה אֶלָּא תַּרְעוֹמֶת.
phrases.english: they have nothing against each other except a complaint.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings proof for the new reading given in step 4

steps.title: When workers already came: full wages, minus the value of resting
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits its ruling to when the workers had not yet gone out. If they went and found no work, the employer pays their wages, but at the lower rate of someone who did not have to work.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? When they did not go out. But if donkey drivers went and found no grain to carry, or workers went and found the field too wet, the employer pays them their wages in full. Still, someone who comes back loaded is not the same as someone who comes back empty, and someone who works is not the same as someone who sits idle.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and shows that its case was about backing out. It also teaches what happens if the workers already came for the job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Only a complaint' applies when the deal fell apart before anyone went out, which is a case of backing out. That confirms the meaning of 'deceived.' If the workers already showed up, the employer must pay, though the amount is reduced because they were spared the actual labor.

keyTerms.meaning: When is this said? (limits a ruling)
Donkey drivers
Workers, laborers
In full
Sitting idle

steps.whatToRemember: 'Deceived' in this ברייתא means backing out. If no one went out yet, there is only a complaint. If the workers already came and found no work, they get paid, but at the reduced rate of an idle worker.

phrases.english: When is this said? When they did not go.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָלְכוּ חַמָּרִים וְלֹא מָצְאוּ תְּבוּאָה,
phrases.english: But if donkey drivers went and did not find grain,
or workers [went] and found the field when it was wet –
he gives them their wages in full,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה הַבָּא טָעוּן לַבָּא רֵיקָן,
phrases.english: but one who comes loaded is not like one who comes empty,
[and] one who does work is not like one who sits idle.
phrases.notes: So he pays them less than the agreed amount, since they didn't actually work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, limiting its ruling and adding the case where the workers already went out
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא's 'deceived' case is about backing out before going out
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's own limit: 'when they did not go'
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule for employment: a worker who shows up and finds no work is still owed pay, but at a reduced rate.

steps.title: Workers who already started are paid for what they did
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the rule of 'only a complaint' to workers who never started. If they started and then quit, the court values the work they finished, for example half a field reaped or half a garment woven.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this rule apply? When they had not started working. But if they had started working, we value what they did for them. How so? They took a field of standing grain to reap for two סלעים, reaped half, and left half. Or they took a garment to weave for two סלעים, wove half, and left half. We value what they did for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going and adds another limit. The rule that the employer has only a complaint applies only when the workers had not started yet. If they started and then quit, they get paid for the work they finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 dealt with workers who went out and found no work. This line moves to workers who began a job and stopped halfway. Their finished work has real value, so the court estimates it and pays them for it. The next steps explain exactly how that estimate works.

keyTerms.meaning: When does this rule apply? A phrase that narrows an earlier rule
They began the work
We estimate the value (the court makes an appraisal)
Standing grain, still in the field
How so? Introduces an example

phrases.english: In what case is this said?
phrases.notes: He means the rule from before: if the workers back out, the employer has only a complaint.

phrases.english: When they had not started the work,
but if they had started the work –
we appraise for them what they did.
How so?
They took on standing grain to reap for two sela,
they reaped half of it and left half of it.
A garment to weave for two sela,
they wove half of it and left half of it –
we appraise for them what they did.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים? שֶׁלֹּא הִתְחִילוּ בִּמְלָאכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit to the ברייתא's 'only a complaint' rule. This one covers workers who started the job and then quit.
steps.raayaObject: How the ברייתא handles workers who back out (חזרו), continuing the reading from step 4

steps.title: How the finished half is valued when prices change
steps.stepSummary: If the half they finished is now worth six דינרים, the employer gives them one סלע, or they can finish and take the full two סלעים. If it is worth one סלע, he gives them one סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was worth six דינרים, he gives them a סלע, or they finish their work and take two סלעים. And if it was worth a סלע, he gives them a סלע.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows how the appraisal works in numbers. The workers who quit do not gain from a rise in prices. They get their original share, or they can finish the job for the agreed full price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סלע is four דינרים. Half the job was originally worth one סלע, half of two סלעים. Even if that half is now worth six דינרים, the workers still get only one סלע, because they were the ones who backed out. The last line ('if it was worth a סלע, he gives a סלע') seems obvious, and the גמרא will explain it later.

keyTerms.meaning: Dinars, coins. Four דינרים make one סלע
A coin worth four דינרים
They finish their work

phrases.english: If it was worth six dinars –
phrases.notes: The part they already did is now worth six דינרים, a סלע and a half, because prices went up.

phrases.english: he gives them a sela,
or they finish their work
and take two sela.
And if it was a sela – he gives them a sela.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה יָפֶה שִׁשָּׁה דִּינָרִים – נוֹתֵן לָהֶן סֶלַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains in numbers how the appraisal from step 7 is carried out.
steps.raayaObject: The payment rule for workers who back out partway
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about hiring craftsmen (the תנא קמא's opinion)

steps.title: רבי דוסא values the work still left to do
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא says the court values the work that still needs to be done. If finishing will cost six דינרים, the employer takes that out of the full wage and gives the first workers only a שקל, or they can finish and take two סלעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסא says: we value what still has to be done. If it was worth six דינרים, he gives them a שקל, or they finish their work and take two סלעים. And if it was worth a סלע, he gives them a סלע.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסא disagrees with the first opinion about how to calculate the pay. He looks at what it will cost the employer to finish the job, not at what the workers already did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full agreed wage is two סלעים, which is eight דינרים. If the employer must pay six דינרים to new workers to finish the job, only two דינרים are left for the first workers. Two דינרים is a שקל. This way the employer never loses because the workers quit.

keyTerms.meaning: What still has to be done
Half a סלע, which is two דינרים

phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa says:
we appraise for them what still has to be done,
if it was worth six dinars –
phrases.notes: Here 'it' is the unfinished half. Hiring others to finish it would cost six דינרים.

phrases.english: he gives them a shekel,
phrases.notes: Eight דינרים, the full wage, minus six leaves two. That is a שקל.

phrases.english: or they finish their work
and take two sela.
And if it was a sela – he gives them a sela.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי דּוֹסָא אוֹמֵר: שָׁמִין לָהֶן מַה שֶּׁעָתִיד לְהֵעָשׂוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different way to calculate the same appraisal described in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The appraisal is based on what it costs to finish the job. The first workers receive the full agreed wage minus that cost, and never more than their original share.

steps.title: When stopping the work causes a loss, the employer may hire others or trick the workers
steps.stepSummary: Everything above applies only when nothing is lost by stopping. If the work will be ruined (דבר האבוד), the employer may hire replacements at the first workers' expense, even up to forty or fifty זוז. Or he may 'deceive' them by promising double pay that he does not have to give.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this rule apply? With something that will not be lost. But with something that will be lost, he hires others at their expense, or he deceives them. How does he deceive them? He says to them: 'I agreed with you on a סלע. Come and take two.' And up to how much may he hire at their expense? Up to forty or fifty זוז.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one more limit. The workers are protected only when nothing gets ruined by their quitting. When delay causes real loss, the employer gets strong tools to make sure the job is finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If grain will rot or flax will spoil, the workers who quit are responsible for the extra cost of hiring replacements, even far above their own wage. The employer may also promise them more money to come back, and he does not have to pay it. That is why the ברייתא calls it 'deceiving' them.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that will be lost or ruined if the work stops
He hires others at their (the first workers') expense
He tricks them
I fixed or agreed on (a wage)
A coin equal to a דינר

steps.whatToRemember: Workers may quit. If they had not started, the employer has only a complaint. If they started, they are paid for their work, with the price figured so they don't gain from quitting. But if quitting causes a loss (דבר האבוד), the employer may hire replacements at their expense or trick them into finishing.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'deceive' (מטען) really means tricking the workers with a promise of extra pay. It is not the special 'backed out' meaning the גמרא gave to הטעו in step 4.

phrases.english: In what case is this said?
With something that is not lost,
phrases.notes: Something that won't be ruined if the work waits a bit.

phrases.english: but with something that is lost –
he hires against them or deceives them.
How does he deceive them?
He says to them:
I fixed a sela for you –
come and take two.
And up to how much may he hire against them?
Up to forty or fifty zuz.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים? בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵין אָבוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the payment rules of steps 7–9 to cases where stopping causes no loss. It gives the employer extra rights when there is a loss.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a דבר האבוד, workers who quit may be charged for replacements, up to forty or fifty זוז, or may be tricked with a promise of extra pay that the employer does not have to keep.

steps.title: The special remedies apply only when no other workers are available
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the harsh remedies of the previous step. They apply only when no replacement workers can be found. If replacements are available and the quitting workers say 'go hire them,' the employer has only a complaint.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this apply? When there are no other workers there to hire. But if there are workers there to hire, and the quitting workers said, 'Go and hire from these,' the employer has only a complaint against them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא puts a limit on the previous rule. The employer may charge the quitters for replacements, or trick them with promised extra pay, only when no other workers can be found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Those strong steps exist only because the employer would otherwise lose his work, a דבר האבוד. If other workers are on hand, he can avoid the loss himself. So he goes back to having only a moral complaint (תרעומת) against the workers who quit.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? A phrase that introduces a limit on a ruling
A complaint or grievance, with no money owed
Workers available to hire

steps.whatToRemember: The employer may hire replacements at the quitters' expense, or trick them, only when the work would be ruined AND no other workers are available.

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
phrases.notes: This points back to the previous step: hiring replacements at the workers' cost, or promising them pay he doesn't have to give.

phrases.english: When there are no workers there to hire.
But if there are workers there to hire,
and they said: "Go out and hire from these"
he has against them nothing but a complaint.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the remedies allowed in step 10 to cases where no replacements are available.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Charging the quitters for replacements, or tricking them, is allowed only when no other workers can be hired. Otherwise the employer has only a complaint.

steps.title: A תנא recites to רב that idle workers get full wages
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites the ברייתא before רב in this form: workers who arrived and found no work receive their full wages.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רב: The employer gives them their wages in full.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier ruling about workers who showed up and found no work. Here a תנא recites it to רב as 'full wages.' This sets up רב's objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תנא in this sense is a person whose job was to memorize and recite ברייתות. His wording says the workers get their whole wage, even though they did nothing. That surprising wording is what רב is about to challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, a person who memorized and recited ברייתות in the study hall
Their wages in full

phrases.english: A tanna taught before Rav:
He gives them their wages in full.
phrases.notes: This is the case from step 6: workers who went out and found no work to do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the step 6 case of workers who found no work and presents a recitation of it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Workers who came and found no work receive their full wages.

steps.title: רב objects in the name of his uncle: only an idle worker's wage
steps.stepSummary: רב tells the תנא that his uncle רבי חייא said he would pay such workers only an idle worker's wage, not full wages.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: My uncle said, 'If I were judging, I would give them only the wage of an idle worker.' And you say he gives them their full wages?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב challenges the תנא's wording. He uses the opinion of his uncle, רבי חייא, who would pay only the lower 'idle worker' rate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An idle worker's wage is the smaller amount a person would accept to sit and do nothing, instead of doing hard work. רב cannot accept that the workers would get the whole wage. That clashes with רבי חייא's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: My uncle. רב's name for רבי חייא
An idle worker. The lower pay for someone who sits without working
If I were the one deciding

phrases.english: He said to him: My uncle said,
phrases.notes: "My uncle" here is רבי חייא, רב's uncle.

phrases.english: If I were the one judging
I would not give them
anything except like an idle worker,
and you say
he gives them their wages in full!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the full-wage recitation of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא's recitation that idle workers get full wages
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חייא, a major authority, would give only an idle worker's wage. So full wages seems wrong.

steps.title: But the ברייתא itself says they get less
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רב's objection. The same ברייתא goes on to say that a worker who did nothing is not paid like one who worked, so it also gives only an idle worker's wage.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches about this very case: One who comes back loaded is not like one who comes back empty, and one who does work is not like one who sits idle!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב argued at all. The ending of the same ברייתא already agrees that the workers get only an idle worker's wage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'full wages' could make it sound like the ברייתא pays everything. But its next line says a person sitting idle is not like a person working. So the ברייתא and רבי חייא seem to say the same thing, and רב's objection looks pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches about this very case. Brings a line from the same source
Loaded, carrying a load
Empty-handed

phrases.english: But it teaches about this very case:
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same ברייתא, the line already given in step 6.

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה הַבָּא טָעוּן לְהַבָּא רֵיקָן,
phrases.english: One who comes loaded is not like one who comes empty,
one who does work is not like one who sits idle!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's objection in step 13 by quoting the end of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא already limits the pay to the idle-worker rate, so there is nothing to object to.

steps.title: The תנא did not finish reciting it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תנא stopped before reciting the ending of the ברייתא. רב only heard 'full wages' and objected to that.
steps.simpleTranslation: They did not finish reciting it before him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב's objection. He heard only the first part of the ברייתא, without the line that lowers the pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב was not disagreeing with the full ברייתא. He was reacting to an incomplete recitation. With the ending included, the ברייתא and רבי חייא agree.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not finish it in front of him

phrases.english: They did not finish it before him.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual explanation of how the recitation happened
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב argued against a ברייתא that already agreed with him.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב heard only part of the ברייתא. The complete ברייתא agrees with רבי חייא.
steps.whatToRemember: In this first version, the ברייתא and רבי חייא both pay an idle worker's wage. רב's objection came from hearing only half the text.

steps.title: Second version: רבי חייא would pay nothing at all
steps.stepSummary: Another version says the תנא did finish the ברייתא. In this version רב objected that רבי חייא would pay nothing at all, while the ברייתא pays an idle worker's wage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: They did finish it before him, and this is what רב was saying. My uncle said, 'If I were judging, I would not give him anything at all.' And you say he gets an idle worker's wage?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different account of the conversation. In this account רב knew the whole ברייתא, but רבי חייא's opinion was even stricter than it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This removes the problem of step 14 in a new way. רב's objection was about the ending itself: paying any wage at all. Now the ברייתא (idle worker's pay) and רבי חייא (no pay) really do disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: At all

phrases.english: There are those who say:
they did finish it before him,
and this is what he was saying.
My uncle said: If I were the one judging
I would not give him anything at all,
and you say like an idle worker!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to step 14. It changes what רב's objection was about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the content of רב's objection
steps.terutzMaskana: רב objected to any payment, because רבי חייא would pay nothing.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In the first, רבי חייא pays an idle worker's wage. In the second, he pays nothing at all.

steps.title: Then the ברייתא and רבי חייא contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: In this second version, the גמרא points out a problem. The ברייתא says to pay an idle worker's wage, and רבי חייא says to pay nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a difficulty with the second version. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two respected sources now disagree on the same case: some pay against no pay. The גמרא wants to show that they are not really arguing.

keyTerms.meaning: But then this is difficult

phrases.english: But then this is difficult.
phrases.notes: The difficulty is that the ברייתא pays an idle worker's wage while רבי חייא pays nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out the contradiction created by the second version in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conflict between the ברייתא and רבי חייא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same case cannot have both an idle worker's wage and no pay at all.

steps.title: It depends on whether the employer checked his field the night before
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles the conflict. רבי חייא, who pays nothing, speaks of an employer who checked his land the night before. The ברייתא, which pays an idle worker's wage, speaks of an employer who did not check.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is where he checked his land the night before. That one is where he did not check his land the night before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by splitting it into two different cases. The question is whether the employer looked at his field the evening before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the employer checked and the field was ready, he did his part. Whatever happened overnight is the workers' bad luck, so he pays nothing. If he never checked, the lack of work is his fault, so he pays them at least an idle worker's wage.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. Opens an answer
He checked his land
The evening, the night before

steps.whatToRemember: Workers who arrive and find no work: if the employer checked his field the night before, he pays nothing. If he did not check, he pays an idle worker's wage.
steps.whyThisMatters: The employer's duty to pay depends on whether he took reasonable care. If he did his part, the loss falls on the workers. If he was careless, he carries it.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is where he checked his land the night before,
phrases.notes: "This one" is רבי חייא's ruling that they get nothing.

phrases.english: that one is where he did not check his land the night before.
phrases.notes: "That one" is the ברייתא, which gives them an idle worker's wage.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דְּסַיְּירַהּ לְאַרְעֵיהּ מִדְּאוּרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of step 17 by separating the two cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case into two situations (הא בהא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and רבי חייא disagree about the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי חייא speaks of an employer who checked his field, so he pays nothing. The ברייתא speaks of one who did not check, so he pays an idle worker's wage.

steps.title: רבא's parallel case: rain floods the field before the workers can plow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the distinction from Step 18 by citing רבא. He describes an employer who hired workers to plow, and then rain flooded the field. His ruling depends on whether the employer checked his land the night before.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רבא said: Someone hired workers to plow. Rain came and filled the field with water, so they could not work. If he had checked his land the night before...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבא's statement, which uses the same 'did he check the night before' split as Step 18. This line only sets up the case and the condition; the ruling comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 18 the גמרא resolved the conflict by saying the law depends on whether the employer checked his field. רבא's case shows this is a known distinction, not something made up just to answer the question. The words 'if he checked his land the night before' are the key condition. What follows from it comes at the start of the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: This is like that which [someone] said. It introduces a parallel teaching that backs up what was just said.
Hired workers
To plow or till the ground
Rain
He checked or inspected it
From the evening before, meaning the night before the work day

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop at 'if he checked his land.' This is only the condition. רבא's actual ruling, and the opposite case where he did not check, continue on the next amud.

phrases.english: This is like that which רבא said:
One who hired workers to plow
and rain came and filled it with water,
if he checked his land the night before –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel statement of רבא that uses the same distinction (checked the land the night before or not) that Step 18 used to settle the conflict.
steps.raayaObject: The distinction from Step 18: an employer who checked his land the night before is treated differently from one who did not.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's ruling about workers hired to plow when rain flooded the field, which depends on whether the employer checked his land the night before.
